title: Real task flat at ~71%; tuning the pilot on the final task
text:
Run F (20 flights per network) in 'boulder, gusts': the champion on 100 fresh real-task flights every 5 generations, gens 245-325: 59% to 80%, about 71% on average, no trend; the pilot lands ~77%. Stage-world checks reach 92-98% but fail on 1-2% boulder hits. So NEAT keeps the start network's skill but hasn't improved on it, with 10 or 20 flights per network.
The start network is what decides the result so far, and the pilot it copies was tuned on half wind / half boulder flights, not the final task. Side experiment (F keeps running): CMA-ES tunes the pilot's 13 gains on the final task only (40 rounds x 16 candidates x 160 flights, seeds 600M+). If it clearly beats the current pilot on paired analysis flights, the next attempt re-clones from it.

title: Finding: the drift sensor mostly feels the lander's own thrust
text:
Building the 'How it sees' page, I plotted the true wind force (hidden from the lander) against its drift sensor over a whole flight. The sensor swings between about -3 and +3 while the true wind stays within +-1 (in units of a full gust). The sensor leaves out side-engine steps but keeps main-engine steps, so when the lander is tilted its own main engine dominates the reading. It is a 'total sideways push' accelerometer, not a wind estimate.
It still helped the pilot (72% -> 94%), but a cleaner sensor would subtract the known sideways thrust of the main engine (from the tilt and the action). A candidate change if progress stalls; not changed now (one change at a time).

title: Rehearsal keeps the boulder skill; selection noise stops progress. Attempt F
text:
Run E (curriculum around the boulder, 40% real-task rehearsal) stage 1 hit its cap: best fresh check 96% landed but 3% boulder hits (the pass needs 0).
Paired on 400 unseen real-task flights: gen 75 champion 76.2%, gen 140 70.0%, pilot 76.8%. So rehearsal works in part: D had fallen to 38%, E stays near the pilot. But it doesn't pass the pilot, and full-wind skill still slipped (gen 140: 80.0% vs pilot 92.3%).
Failure breakdown (gen 75, real task): crashed 12.8%, boulder 7.0%, off-pad 5.8%, timeout 1.8%; the pilot: off-pad 10.5%, boulder 7.0%, crashed 6.8%.
Diagnosis: with 10 flights per network, 4 of them real, selection can't tell 76% from 70%; later champions looked better on the stage world but were worse on the real one.
Change (one): attempt F resumes E's population at the start of stage 2 with 20 flights per network and the top 8 re-flown on 60.

note: Attempt F = E resumed at the start of stage 2 (gen ~152), with one change: 20 training flights per network instead of 10, and the top 8 re-flown on 60 instead of 40. Why: in the real task E's champions did not pass the pilot and drifted down (gen 75: 76.2%, gen 140: 70.0%, pilot 76.8%, 400 paired flights) while their stage-world checks rose: selection on 10 flights (4 of them real) is mostly luck.

expect: Steering around the boulder while gusts push sideways. Pass at 93%.
Steering around the boulder while gusts push sideways. Pass at 93%.

note: Attempt E: the curriculum rebuilt around what the network can't do yet. Run D showed the easy stages destroy skill the exact copy already has (full wind: 90% at gen 0, 79% after calm air, 52% after the steady push; boulder 71% -> 38%), because selection only sees the easy world. So: start from the exact copy, train the weakness (the boulder) from calm air up to full wind, and fly 40% of every stage's training flights in the full final world (rehearsal) so nothing is forgotten.

expect: The pilot lands 95.6% here. The copy should get there; selection now sees the boulder in every flight.

title: The easy stages were erasing skill. Attempt E: curriculum around the weakness, with rehearsal
text:
Run D passed calm air (gen 5) and the steady push (gen 91, 90% / 91%). But paired against the pilot on 300 unseen flights, D's champions got WORSE at the real task as the stages went on:
  full wind: gen 0 90.3% (pilot 92.3%), gen 5 78.7%, gen 91 52.0%
  with the boulder: gen 0 71.0% (pilot 76.7%), gen 91 38.0%
Selection only sees the stage's easy world, so mutations erode the hard-world skill with nothing to stop them. A curriculum that helps a beginner hurts an expert start.
Attempt E (one change: the curriculum): restart from the exact copy; train the weakness, the boulder, from calm air up (boulder in calm air -> boulder in gusts -> everything -> polish); and fly 40% of every stage's training flights in the full final world (rehearsal), so selection always sees the real task.

expect: Real gusts at full strength. The wind project's best NEAT reached ~91% with turbulence; aim 95% without.
Lean into a constant push that grows from 5 to 15. The pilot lands ~84-90% here, so pass at 90%. Risk: landing off the pad downwind.

note: Attempt D: restart forced by a bug. Runs A-C started from a broken copy of the pilot: NEAT's tanh output squashed the cloned scores to ties, so 1 step in 9 took the wrong action (the copy landed 43% in wind instead of 92%). Fixed (identity outputs, test). Restarting, so three more changes ride along: the 15-input clone (+2 route sensors), seed noise 0.02 and weight mutation power 0.05 (the boulder skill is fragile: noise 0.05 cost ~10 points), and 30% boulder flights mixed into stages 1-4 so selection keeps protecting the boulder skill (forgotten twice before). The exact start network: 98% wind, 77% boulder (60 flights each).

expect: Pass at once: the exact copy of the pilot lands nearly every calm flight.

title: Bug found: NEAT started from a broken copy. Attempt D
text:
While checking why the boulder skill was missing, I compared the cloned network flown directly with the same network converted into a NEAT genome. With the boulder: 71% vs 30%. In wind: 92% vs 43%. The conversion was not exact: NEAT's tanh output neurons squashed the cloned action scores (up to +-20) to exactly 1.0, and the first of a tie won. About 1 step in 9 took the wrong action. The unit test missed it because a random small network never saturates.
Correction: episode 1 said NEAT started from a copy landing ~82%. The genome NEAT actually got was much worse; runs A-C's stage results are real measurements, but they were achieved from a broken start.
Fix: identity output neurons (exact copy), test now uses realistic weights and fails without the fix. The exact 15-input copy: 98% wind, 77% boulder (60 flights each, rough).
Attempt D restarts from it, with three changes riding along on the forced restart: 2 route sensors (15 inputs), gentler mutation (seed noise 0.02, weight power 0.05: noise 0.05 cost ~10 points with the boulder), and 30% boulder flights mixed into stages 1-4.

expect: Everything on, only the env score + landing bonus. Pass = 98% on 100 + 100 fresh flights, then the 1,000-flight goal check.
Starts near 14-25% landed with full-size boulders, so ramp the size 40% -> 100% over 150 generations. Expect the longest stage; a pass at 95% may need the polish stage too.

title: Gusts passed; full wind below the pilot; boulder skill missing; attempt C
text:
Gusts (no turbulence) passed at generation 202: 96% on 100 fresh flights, confirmed.
Full wind (gusts 15 + turbulence 1.5): the best fresh check was 92% (gen 373), but that was partly selection luck. On 400 paired unseen flights the same champion lands 86.0% vs the pilot's 91.0% (-5.0 [-9.2, -0.8]). The gusts champion: 71.8%. So turbulence is the hard part of the wind, and NEAT is still below its teacher there.
Bigger problem, found by checking ahead: with the boulder, the best champion lands 14.3% and even the cloned start network only 25.0%, vs the pilot's 76.7% (300 paired flights). The boulder rules (steer beside it, stay above it) never made it into the clone.
Change (one): attempt C resumes B's population at gen 417 and ramps the boulder size from 40% to 100% over the first half of the boulder stage, the way wind was ramped.

note: Attempt C = B resumed from its population at gen ~412 (in the gusts + turbulence stage), with one change: the boulder stage ramps the boulder size from 40% to 100%. Why: the cloned start network only landed 25% with the boulder (pilot 77%) and B's best wind champion 14% (300 paired flights): the boulder skill was never cloned well, so it must be learned in NEAT, from small boulders up.

expect: The full wind task. Beat the earlier 91%.
The full wind task. Beat the earlier 91%.

title: Steady push passed, beating the pilot, but it forgot the gusts
text:
Run B passed the steady-push stage at generation 76: 99% landed on 100 fresh flights, 96% on the confirmation.
Paired with the hand-written pilot on the same 300 unseen flights against a full-strength constant push: champion 97.3%, pilot 82.3%, difference +15.0 points [95% CI +10.7, +19.3]. NEAT beat its teacher.
But in the real gusty wind with turbulence the same champion lands only 64.3% vs the pilot's 92.3% (-28.0 [-34.0, -22.0]): it specialised in a constant push. The gusts stage (now running, wind ramping 5 -> 15) has to win that back. If it doesn't, the steady-push stage should be shortened or mixed with real gusts.

title: Attempt A stopped, B started: a bug and weaker training wheels
text:
Run A passed calm air at generation 5 (98% and 97% on two fresh sets of 100), but in the steady-push stage the champion fell to 72-80% landed already at 'wind 5'. Two causes, both measured with the pilot on 200 flights:
1. A bug: the steady push ignored the wind ramp and was always 30-100% of full strength. Fixed, with a test.
2. Training wheels at full strength hurt: the pilot landed 83% with them, 84% without, 89.5% at 0.3 strength. They stop the lander tilting to steer.
Attempt B: wheels start at 0.3, steady-push pass at 90%. Restarted from the cloned network (stage 1 took only 3 minutes).

expect: The drift sensor should let it lean into a constant push. Risk: landing off the pad downwind.

title: Kickoff: NEAT seeded with a cloned pilot
text:
Goal: >= 98% landed between the flags on 1,000 unseen flights with wind 15, turbulence 1.5 and a floating boulder, by Wednesday 4 November 18:00.

Built today: the world (wind seeded per flight, the boulder as a static rock, training wheels), a hand-written pilot tuned with CMA-ES (500 unseen flights: calm 100% landed, wind+turbulence 93.8%, with the boulder 74.2%), and a 13-24-4 network cloned from it with DAgger (about 82% landed over mixed worlds). Every genome in NEAT's first population is a copy of that network with small noise; its 24 hidden neurons are protected from deletion.

Run A started: six stages (calm, steady push, gusts, turbulence, boulder, polish). Generation 0 already landed 99% on 100 fresh calm flights.

note: NEAT from a cloned teacher network (24 hidden), six stages: calm, steady push, gusts, turbulence, boulder, polish. Training wheels fade in stages 2-4.

expect: Quick: the cloned network already lands in calm air; NEAT polishes centring. Pass within ~30 generations.
